# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
```

### Using asdf

```
asdf plugin add richgo
asdf install richgo 0.3.6
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
  blinkSlow: (true | false)
  blinkRapid: (true | false)
  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
  inverse: (true | false)
  conceal: (true | false)
  crossOut: (true | false)
  frame: (true | false)
  encircle: (true | false)
  overline: (true | false)
  # Fore-color of text
  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
  # Back-color of text
  background: # Same format as `foreground`

# Style of the "Start" lines.
startStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" lines.
passStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" lines.
failStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Skip" lines.
skipStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "File" lines.
fileStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Line" lines.
lineStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
passPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
failPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# A threshold of the coverage
coverThreshold: (0-100)

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
coveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
uncoveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
removals:
  - (regexp)
# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
```

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
```

### Using asdf

```
asdf plugin add richgo
asdf install richgo 0.3.6
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
  blinkSlow: (true | false)
  blinkRapid: (true | false)
  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
  inverse: (true | false)
  conceal: (true | false)
  crossOut: (true | false)
  frame: (true | false)
  encircle: (true | false)
  overline: (true | false)
  # Fore-color of text
  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
  # Back-color of text
  background: # Same format as `foreground`

# Style of the "Start" lines.
startStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" lines.
passStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" lines.
failStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Skip" lines.
skipStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "File" lines.
fileStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Line" lines.
lineStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
passPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
failPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# A threshold of the coverage
coverThreshold: (0-100)

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
coveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
uncoveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
removals:
  - (regexp)
# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
```

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

### Default configuration

```yaml
labelType: long
buildStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
startStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passStyle:
  foreground: green
failStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
skipStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passPackageStyle:
  foreground: green
  hide: true
failPackageStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
  hide: true
coverThreshold: 50
coveredStyle:
  foreground: green
uncoveredStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
fileStyle:
  foreground: cyan
lineStyle:
  foreground: magenta
```

### Solarized Dark theme compatibility

The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.

To resolve that conflict, you can set another color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle" in your `.richstyle` file:

```yaml
startStyle:
  foreground: yellow

skipStyle:
  foreground: lightYellow
```

## Overriding colorization detection

By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.

To force colorization, add `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` to the environment:

```sh
RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 richgo test ./... | tee test.log
```

## Getting the version

If you want to get the version of `richgo`, this information is embedded in the binary (since Go 1.18). You can view it with `go version -m`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo)
./richgo: go1.18
	path	github.com/kyoh86/richgo
	mod	github.com/kyoh86/richgo	v0.3.10	h1:iSGvcjhtQN2IVrBDhPk0if0R/RMQnCN1E/9OyAW4UUs=
	[...]
```

With POSIX `awk`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo) | awk '$1 == "mod" && $2 == "github.com/kyoh86/richgo" {print $3;}'
v0.3.10
```

def run_pty(args, inp, env=None, stdout_tty=True, stderr_tty=False):
    # create pty pair for stdout
    master_out, slave_out = pty.openpty() if stdout_tty else (None, subprocess.PIPE)
    master_err, slave_err = pty.openpty() if stderr_tty else (None, subprocess.PIPE)
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=slave_out, stderr=slave_err, env=e, close_fds=True)

    p.stdin.write(inp.encode()); p.stdin.close()
    out=b""
    if stdout_tty:
        while True:
            try:
                r,_,_=select.select([master_out],[],[],0.5)
                if not r: 
                    if p.poll() is not None: break
                    else: continue
                data=os.read(master_out, 8192)
                if not data: break

import pty, os, subprocess, select, threading

def read_all(fd, buf_list):
    while True:
        try:
            data=os.read(fd, 8192)
            if not data: break
            buf_list.append(data)
        except OSError:
            break

def test(stdout_tty, stderr_tty, env_extra=None):
    sample=b"=== RUN   TestSampleOK\n--- PASS: TestSampleOK (0.00s)\nPASS\nok   \texample.com/foo\t0.123s\nhello\n"
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    # setup stdout
    if stdout_tty:
        m_out, s_out = pty.openpty()
        stdout_target=s_out
    else:
        r_out, w_out = os.pipe()
        stdout_target=w_out
        m_out=r_out
    if stderr_tty:
        m_err, s_err = pty.openpty()
        stderr_target=s_err
    else:
        r_err, w_err = os.pipe()
        stderr_target=w_err
        m_err=r_err
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable","testfilter"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=stdout_target, stderr=stderr_target, env=env)
    # close slave ends in parent
    os.close(stdout_target); os.close(stderr_target)
    out_chunks=[]; err_chunks=[]
    t1=threading.Thread(target=read_all, args=(m_out,out_chunks), daemon=True)
    t2=threading.Thread(target=read_all, args=(m_err,err_chunks), daemon=True)
    t1.start(); t2.start()
    p.stdin.write(sample); p.stdin.close()
    p.wait()
    t1.join(2); t2.join(2)
    try: os.close(m_out)
    except: pass
    try: os.close(m_err)
    except: pass
    print(f"stdout_tty={stdout_tty} stderr_tty={stderr_tty} env={env_extra} exit={p.returncode}")
    print("  stdout:", repr(b''.join(out_chunks)))
    print("  stderr:", repr(b''.join(err_chunks)))

test(False, False)
test(True, False)
test(False, True)
test(True, True)
test(False, False, {"RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR":"1"})
test(False, False, {"RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR":"0"})
test(False, False, {"RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR":""})
PY"}

import pty, os, subprocess, threading
def read_all(fd, buf):
    while True:
        try:
            d=os.read(fd,8192)
            if not d: break
            buf.append(d)
        except OSError: break

def test(cmd, stdout_tty, stderr_tty, env_extra=None, inp=b""):
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    if stdout_tty:
        m_out,s_out=pty.openpty(); out_t=s_out
    else:
        r,w=os.pipe(); m_out=r; out_t=w
    if stderr_tty:
        m_err,s_err=pty.openpty(); err_t=s_err
    else:
        r,w=os.pipe(); m_err=r; err_t=w
    p=subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=out_t, stderr=err_t, env=env)
    os.close(out_t); os.close(err_t)
    oc=[]; ec=[]
    t1=threading.Thread(target=read_all,args=(m_out,oc)); t2=threading.Thread(target=read_all,args=(m_err,ec))
    t1.start(); t2.start()
    if inp: p.stdin.write(inp)
    p.stdin.close(); p.wait(); t1.join(2); t2.join(2)
    print(cmd, stdout_tty, stderr_tty, "exit",p.returncode)
    print(" out",b''.join(oc))
    print(" err",b''.join(ec))

def run(extra, cwd="/tmp/loc_cwd2"):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update({"RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR":"1","GOROOT":"/tmp/loc_empty"})

    for k,v in extra.items():
        if v is None: e.pop(k,None)
        else: e[k]=v
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","testfilter"], input=b"--- PASS: TestA (0s)\n", capture_output=True, env=e, cwd=cwd)

run({})
run({"HOME":"/tmp/loc_empty"})

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from mkcfg_probe import run_cfg

    run_cfg(f"passStyle:\n  {a}: true\n" if a.lower() not in("foreground",) else f"passStyle:\n  {a}: blue\n", b"--- PASS: TestA (0s)\n")
PY"}

// Wait waits for the command to exit and waits for any copying to
// stdin or copying from stdout or stderr to complete.
//
// The command must have been started by Start.
//
// The returned error is nil if the command runs, has no problems
// copying stdin, stdout, and stderr, and exits with a zero exit
// status.
//
// If the command fails to run or doesn't complete successfully, the
// error is of type *ExitError. Other error types may be
// returned for I/O problems.
//
// If any of c.Stdin, c.Stdout or c.Stderr are not an *os.File, Wait also waits
// for the respective I/O loop copying to or from the process to complete.
//
// Wait releases any resources associated with the Cmd.
func (c *Cmd) Wait() error {
	if c.Process == nil {
		return errors.New("exec: not started")
	}
	if c.ProcessState != nil {
		return errors.New("exec: Wait was already called")
	}

	state, err := c.Process.Wait()
	if err == nil && !state.Success() {
		err = &ExitError{ProcessState: state}
	}
	c.ProcessState = state

	var timer *time.Timer
	if c.ctxResult != nil {
		watch := <-c.ctxResult
		timer = watch.timer
		// If c.Process.Wait returned an error, prefer that.
		// Otherwise, report any error from the watchCtx goroutine,
		// such as a Context cancellation or a WaitDelay overrun.
		if err == nil && watch.err != nil {
			err = watch.err
		}
	}

	if goroutineErr := c.awaitGoroutines(timer); err == nil {
		// Report an error from the copying goroutines only if the program otherwise
		// exited normally on its own. Otherwise, the copying error may be due to the
		// abnormal termination.
		err = goroutineErr
	}
	closeDescriptors(c.parentIOPipes)
	c.parentIOPipes = nil

	return err
}

package editor

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strings"
)

// Editor transforms one complete line (always presented with a trailing
// newline) into the exact bytes that should be written out.
type Editor interface {
	Edit(string) string
}

// EditFunc adapts a plain function to the Editor interface.
type EditFunc func(string) string

func (f EditFunc) Edit(line string) string { return f(line) }

// Raw returns an editor that passes lines through, apart from removing
// a single carriage return in front of the trailing newline.
func Raw() Editor {
	return EditFunc(func(line string) string {
		return strings.Replace(line, "\r\n", "\n", 1)
	})
}

// stream is an io.WriteCloser that reassembles lines from arbitrary
// write chunks and feeds them to an Editor one at a time.
type stream struct {
	out    io.Writer
	editor Editor
	rest   []byte
}

// NewStream creates a line-buffering writer around out.
func NewStream(out io.Writer, editor Editor) io.WriteCloser {
	return &stream{out: out, editor: editor}
}

func (s *stream) writeLines(lines [][]byte) {
	for _, line := range lines {
		edited := s.editor.Edit(string(line) + "\n")
		if edited == "" {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Fprint(s.out, edited)
	}
}

func (s *stream) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	data := append(s.rest, p...)
	parts := bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n"))
	s.rest = parts[len(parts)-1]
	s.writeLines(parts[:len(parts)-1])
	return len(p), nil
}

func (s *stream) Close() error {
	s.writeLines([][]byte{s.rest})
	s.rest = nil
	return nil
}
